newsitem.title: CHINA: Dow Corning mulls China as site for future plant.
newsitem.headline: Dow Corning mulls China as site for future plant.

text.p: U.S. company Dow Corning Corp is considering China as a possible site for a $500 million-plant to produce the basic material needed for silicone production, the company chief said on Friday.
"We're engaged in an effort on where that plant will go," said Richard Hazleton, Dow Corning's chairman and chief executive officer. "China is one of the places on the candidate list for that."

The company will decide by the end of this year where to base the Asian plant -- China's Tianjin city, Malaysia or Korea. It currently has two other "basic plants" worldwide, one in the U.S. and one in Britain.
The plant will produce monomers, chemical building-blocks used in the production of silicone.

Although Dow Corning, a joint venture between Dow Chemical and Corning Inc, is currently operating under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States, Hazleton said it had not affected business or investment plans.
The company filed for bankruptcy protection two years ago, freezing litigation against it, due to lawsuits that allege the company's silicone-gel breast implants caused health problems.
"We are proceeding through the Chapter 11 process as a way to reach a fair resolution, not only for us but for the claimants," Hazleton said.
"In the meantime, our business has remained very healthy," he said. "It really has no effect at all that we can detect on our on-going business."
Dow Corning's worldwide sales were around $2.5 billion in 1996 with 60 percent outside of the U.S. and 30 percent in Asia alone.
The company on Friday opened a $30 million-manufacturing facility in Shanghai -- its first in China -- to produce silicone emulsions and sealants.
